## Results
# Bedrock cost analysis, account 123456789012 (us-east-1)

**Cost Explorer doesn't show Bedrock inference costs tripling. The only real increase is a new AgentCore charge that appeared on one day, 2026-11-16.**

## Confirmed findings

**1. Total Bedrock cost is tiny.** These figures come from Cost Explorer (CE) and are all marked "Estimated".

| Service line | Baseline 11-09 to 11-15 | Incident 11-16 to 11-22 |
|---|---|---|
| Amazon Bedrock (model inference) | $0.4035 | $0.0453 (down about 89%) |
| Amazon Bedrock Service | $0.0006 | $0.0002 |
| **Amazon Bedrock AgentCore** | **$0** | **$13.0567 (new)** |
| Bedrock family total | $0.404 | $13.10 |

- The "tripling" the user sees is almost certainly the AgentCore line. It went from $0 to $13.06, which is much more than 3x.
- Other lines that moved:
  - GuardDuty rose from $0.002 to $0.78.
  - OpenSearch rose from $6.87 to $11.30.
  - AWSDevOpsAgent, the largest line in the account, fell from $204.54 to $115.02.

**2. The AgentCore cost is a single-day spike.**
- All $13.0567 landed on 2026-11-16. Every other day from 11-17 to 11-23 is $0, and 11-14 and 11-15 are $0 too.
- Usage type `USE1-Runtime:Consumption-based:vCPU` accounts for $13.0567 of it.
- Memory (`Runtime:Consumption-based:Memory`) shows 218.66 GB-hours at $0.
- Gateway API invocations were 144 at $0, and data transfer was a negligible fraction of a cent.

**3. The AgentCore billing doesn't match the usage.**
- CE reports 3.175 vCPU-hours for 11-16 at $13.06. That is about **$4.11 per vCPU-hour**.
- CloudWatch `CPUUsed-vCPUHours` agrees with 3.175 vCPU-hours for 11-16. It is split across five runtimes at about 0.62–0.66 vCPU-hours each:
  - `llmops_eval_orders_agent`
  - `llmops_eval_support_agent`
  - `llmops_eval_billing_agent`
  - `llmops_eval_search_agent`
  - `llmops_eval_catalog_agent`
- From memory, the AgentCore list price is about $0.09 per vCPU-hour. I did not verify that against the pricing page. If it is right, the charge is roughly 45x higher than usage would justify. Memory being $0 while vCPU carries all the cost also looks odd.
- CloudWatch has CPU and memory data only for 11-16. There is no AgentCore runtime activity on any other day in 11-02 to 11-23.
- A runtime metering or billing anomaly is possible. I can't confirm it from the data I can read.

**4. Model inference volume and mix did not grow.**
- CloudWatch `AWS/Bedrock`, summed over all models:

| | Baseline 11-09 to 11-15 | Incident 11-16 to 11-22 |
|---|---|---|
| Invocations | about 5,700 | about 2,650 |
| Input tokens | about 16.7M | about 11.4M |
| Output tokens | about 5.97M | about 2.4M |

- The model invocation log shows 5,694 records in the baseline week and 3,046 in the incident week.
- Client errors were low and flat (19–32 per day, falling to 5 on 11-17). I found no sign of a retry or throttling loop.
- There is no provisioned throughput (`list_provisioned_model_throughputs` returned empty).

**5. Cost is near zero for the models that carry the token volume.**
- The big token consumers are the "mantle" usage types: `claude-sonnet-5` at about 27.8M input and 8.3M output tokens over the two weeks, and `gpt-5.6-terra`. Both show **$0 unblended cost** in CE.
- Their usage was flat or declining week over week.
- Only Nova Lite output tokens (about $0.45 over two weeks) and a few guardrail units carry real cost.

**6. Callers, from the invocation log group `/llmops-demo/bedrock-invocations`.**
- Sonnet 5 callers are interactive `Admin` SSO sessions (`*-session` users).
  - Baseline: user4 was the top caller (1,904 calls, 6.8M input tokens), followed by user1, user6, user2, user5 and user3.
  - Incident week: user2 was top (2,283 calls, 10.8M input tokens), followed by user1 (393) and user3 (94).
  - The caller mix changed, but total volume fell.
- GPT-5.6-terra callers are the `llmops-eval-runner` role from CodeBuild. They make about 31 calls per run with small payloads.
- Nova Lite and Titan callers are the `llmops-lf-*` app and knowledge base roles, at a few calls per day each.
- I found no unknown identities in the top callers. I did not do a source-IP review.

**7. CloudTrail shows no relevant changes in what I could retrieve.**
- AgentCore events for 11-13 to 11-17 were only `monitorAssociationRoleSession` read calls (`ListAgentRuntimes`, `GetAgentRuntime`). Those are the DevOps agent's own calls.
- Bedrock write events 11-09 to 11-23 showed only read calls from the same monitor role.
- I saw no runtime creation, model access change, or provisioned throughput change.

## Hypotheses (not confirmed)
- **Most likely:** The "tripled" figure is the new AgentCore Runtime vCPU charge on 11-16. The five `llmops_eval_*` runtimes were probably exercised on 11-16 as part of an eval or LLMOps test harness. That would also explain the CodeBuild `llmops-eval-runner`. The cost is far above what 3.175 vCPU-hours should cost, so a rate or metering anomaly (or a one-time adjustment) is plausible.
- **Less likely:** The user is comparing against a different view, such as the month-to-date total, or looking at the "$0 cost" mantle usage that may be repriced later. CE flags these figures as estimated, so a later revision is possible.

- Hourly CE data requires an opt-in, which isn't enabled, so I couldn't find the hour of the spike.
- The role lacks `bedrock-agentcore:ListAgentRuntimes`, so I couldn't read runtime configuration (vCPU or memory size, creation date).
- The CloudWatch AgentCore `Sessions` and `Invocations` queries returned no data, probably because of a dimension mismatch. Per-runtime session counts for 11-16 are not verified.
- I didn't check tags or linked accounts. This looks like a single account with no tag allocation visible.

1. Page `lookup_cloudtrail_events` for 11-15 12:00 to 11-17 05:45 on `bedrock-agentcore.amazonaws.com`. Look for `CreateAgentRuntime`, `UpdateAgentRuntime`, `InvokeAgentRuntime` and `CreateGateway`, and note which identities and source IPs appear.

3. Compare the 11-16 vCPU line with the AgentCore pricing page. If the rate is off, open an AWS Support billing case. Re-check CE in a few days, as the figures are estimates.
4. Grant `bedrock-agentcore:ListAgentRuntimes` and `GetAgentRuntime` read permissions, and enable CE hourly granularity if finer detail is wanted.

{"id": "4ab137d3-81a3-4d4d-a634-1218a55ed302", "role": "assistant", "content": [{"text": "# Bedrock cost analysis, account 123456789012 (us-east-1)

**Cost Explorer doesn't show Bedrock inference costs tripling. The only real increase is a new AgentCore charge that appeared on one day, 2026-11-16.**

## Confirmed findings

**1. Total Bedrock cost is tiny.** These figures come from Cost Explorer (CE) and are all marked "Estimated".

| Service line | Baseline 11-09 to 11-15 | Incident 11-16 to 11-22 |
|---|---|---|
| Amazon Bedrock (model inference) | $0.4035 | $0.0453 (down about 89%) |
| Amazon Bedrock Service | $0.0006 | $0.0002 |
| **Amazon Bedrock AgentCore** | **$0** | **$13.0567 (new)** |
| Bedrock family total | $0.404 | $13.10 |

- The "tripling" the user sees is almost certainly the AgentCore line. It went from $0 to $13.06, which is much more than 3x.
- Other lines that moved:
  - GuardDuty rose from $0.002 to $0.78.
  - OpenSearch rose from $6.87 to $11.30.
  - AWSDevOpsAgent, the largest line in the account, fell from $204.54 to $115.02.

**2. The AgentCore cost is a single-day spike.**
- All $13.0567 landed on 2026-11-16. Every other day from 11-17 to 11-23 is $0, and 11-14 and 11-15 are $0 too.
- Usage type `USE1-Runtime:Consumption-based:vCPU` accounts for $13.0567 of it.
- Memory (`Runtime:Consumption-based:Memory`) shows 218.66 GB-hours at $0.
- Gateway API invocations were 144 at $0, and data transfer was a negligible fraction of a cent.

**3. The AgentCore billing doesn't match the usage.**
- CE reports 3.175 vCPU-hours for 11-16 at $13.06. That is about **$4.11 per vCPU-hour**.
- CloudWatch `CPUUsed-vCPUHours` agrees with 3.175 vCPU-hours for 11-16. It is split across five runtimes at about 0.62–0.66 vCPU-hours each:
  - `llmops_eval_orders_agent`
  - `llmops_eval_support_agent`
  - `llmops_eval_billing_agent`
  - `llmops_eval_search_agent`
  - `llmops_eval_catalog_agent`
- From memory, the AgentCore list price is about $0.09 per vCPU-hour. I did not verify that against the pricing page. If it is right, the charge is roughly 45x higher than usage would justify. Memory being $0 while vCPU carries all the cost also looks odd.
- CloudWatch has CPU and memory data only for 11-16. There is no AgentCore runtime activity on any other day in 11-02 to 11-23.
- A runtime metering or billing anomaly is possible. I can't confirm it from the data I can read.

**4. Model inference volume and mix did not grow.**
- CloudWatch `AWS/Bedrock`, summed over all models:

| | Baseline 11-09 to 11-15 | Incident 11-16 to 11-22 |
|---|---|---|
| Invocations | about 5,700 | about 2,650 |
| Input tokens | about 16.7M | about 11.4M |
| Output tokens | about 5.97M | about 2.4M |

- The model invocation log shows 5,694 records in the baseline week and 3,046 in the incident week.
- Client errors were low and flat (19–32 per day, falling to 5 on 11-17). I found no sign of a retry or throttling loop.
- There is no provisioned throughput (`list_provisioned_model_throughputs` returned empty).

**5. Cost is near zero for the models that carry the token volume.**
- The big token consumers are the "mantle" usage types: `claude-sonnet-5` at about 27.8M input and 8.3M output tokens over the two weeks, and `gpt-5.6-terra`. Both show **$0 unblended cost** in CE.
- Their usage was flat or declining week over week.
- Only Nova Lite output tokens (about $0.45 over two weeks) and a few guardrail units carry real cost.

**6. Callers, from the invocation log group `/llmops-demo/bedrock-invocations`.**
- Sonnet 5 callers are interactive `Admin` SSO sessions (`*-session` users).
  - Baseline: user4 was the top caller (1,904 calls, 6.8M input tokens), followed by user1, user6, user2, user5 and user3.
  - Incident week: user2 was top (2,283 calls, 10.8M input tokens), followed by user1 (393) and user3 (94).
  - The caller mix changed, but total volume fell.
- GPT-5.6-terra callers are the `llmops-eval-runner` role from CodeBuild. They make about 31 calls per run with small payloads.
- Nova Lite and Titan callers are the `llmops-lf-*` app and knowledge base roles, at a few calls per day each.
- I found no unknown identities in the top callers. I did not do a source-IP review.

**7. CloudTrail shows no relevant changes in what I could retrieve.**
- AgentCore events for 11-13 to 11-17 were only `monitorAssociationRoleSession` read calls (`ListAgentRuntimes`, `GetAgentRuntime`). Those are the DevOps agent's own calls.
- Bedrock write events 11-09 to 11-23 showed only read calls from the same monitor role.
- I saw no runtime creation, model access change, or provisioned throughput change.

## Hypotheses (not confirmed)
- **Most likely:** The "tripled" figure is the new AgentCore Runtime vCPU charge on 11-16. The five `llmops_eval_*` runtimes were probably exercised on 11-16 as part of an eval or LLMOps test harness. That would also explain the CodeBuild `llmops-eval-runner`. The cost is far above what 3.175 vCPU-hours should cost, so a rate or metering anomaly (or a one-time adjustment) is plausible.
- **Less likely:** The user is comparing against a different view, such as the month-to-date total, or looking at the "$0 cost" mantle usage that may be repriced later. CE flags these figures as estimated, so a later revision is possible.

## Gaps
- **CloudTrail write events were only partly retrieved.** The all-account write lookup returned just 5 events (11-17 05:45–05:56) before the size cap hit. Events from 11-15 12:00 to 11-17 05:45 were not covered, so who exercised the AgentCore runtimes on 11-16 is unconfirmed.
- Hourly CE data requires an opt-in, which isn't enabled, so I couldn't find the hour of the spike.
- The role lacks `bedrock-agentcore:ListAgentRuntimes`, so I couldn't read runtime configuration (vCPU or memory size, creation date).
- The CloudWatch AgentCore `Sessions` and `Invocations` queries returned no data, probably because of a dimension mismatch. Per-runtime session counts for 11-16 are not verified.
- I didn't check tags or linked accounts. This looks like a single account with no tag allocation visible.

## Suggested next steps
1. Page `lookup_cloudtrail_events` for 11-15 12:00 to 11-17 05:45 on `bedrock-agentcore.amazonaws.com`. Look for `CreateAgentRuntime`, `UpdateAgentRuntime`, `InvokeAgentRuntime` and `CreateGateway`, and note which identities and source IPs appear.
2. Look at the AgentCore runtime log groups (`/aws/bedrock-agentcore/runtimes/...`) for the five `llmops_eval_*` runtimes on 11-16, to see which job or test drove them.
3. Compare the 11-16 vCPU line with the AgentCore pricing page. If the rate is off, open an AWS Support billing case. Re-check CE in a few days, as the figures are estimates.
4. Grant `bedrock-agentcore:ListAgentRuntimes` and `GetAgentRuntime` read permissions, and enable CE hourly granularity if finer detail is wanted.
5. Set a Cost Anomaly Detection monitor or AWS Budget on the Bedrock and AgentCore services so future one-day spikes alert.", "type": "text"}], "created_at": null}
